title: Seeds that sprout: a binomial claim and an experiment

stimulus.title: A seed company's claim
stimulus.text: A seed company claims that 80% of its tomato seeds sprout (germinate) when planted. A community garden buys a very large shipment of the seeds. A gardener selects 15 seeds at random from the shipment, plants them in identical conditions, and finds that 8 of the 15 seeds sprout (invented data).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Assume the company's claim is true. Define the random variable of interest in context, identify its probability distribution with the values of its parameters, and justify that distribution.

rubric.point: Defines the random variable as a count in context: X = the number of the 15 randomly selected seeds that sprout.
accept: Let X = the number of seeds, out of the 15 planted, that germinate
A definition that names the count and the 15 seeds; "X = seeds that sprout" alone does not earn the point

rubric.point: Identifies the distribution as binomial with n = 15 and p = 0.8, both parameters stated.
accept: X is binomial, n = 15, p = 0.80
B(15, 0.8) with n and p labeled

rubric.point: Justifies binomial in context: each seed sprouts or does not, the number of seeds is fixed at 15, each seed has the same 0.8 chance, and seeds chosen at random from a very large shipment sprout independently of each other.
accept: All four conditions (two outcomes, fixed n, same p, independent trials) stated in the context of the seeds
Independence must be addressed; listing "BINS" without context does not earn the point

parts.sample: Let X = the number of the 15 randomly selected seeds that sprout. If the claim is true, X is binomial with n = 15 and p = 0.8. Each seed either sprouts or does not (two outcomes), the number of seeds is fixed at 15, each seed has the same probability 0.8 of sprouting, and because the seeds were selected at random from a very large shipment, whether one seed sprouts does not change the chance for another, so the trials are independent.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Assume the company's claim is true. Calculate the probability that 8 or fewer of the 15 seeds sprout. Show your work.

rubric.point: Shows the structure of the calculation: P(X <= 8) for X binomial with n = 15 and p = 0.8, written as a sum of binomial terms, a complement, or a cumulative probability with the distribution, parameters and boundary labeled.
accept: binomcdf with n = 15, p = 0.8, upper bound 8, if the inputs are labeled in words
Calculator syntax alone, with no labels, does not earn the point
any value from 0.0178 to 0.0184 following correct work

parts.sample: X is binomial with n = 15 and p = 0.8. P(X <= 8) = P(X = 0) + P(X = 1) + ... + P(X = 8), where P(X = k) = (15Ck)(0.8)^k(0.2)^(15 - k). Using the binomial cumulative probability with n = 15, p = 0.8 and upper bound 8, P(X <= 8) = 0.0181.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain what your answer to part (b) suggests about the company's claim.

rubric.point: Interprets the probability conditionally: if the claim (80%) is true, the chance of 8 or fewer sprouting out of 15 is about 0.018.
accept: Assuming 80% of seeds sprout, getting 8 or fewer of 15 would happen about 1.8% of the time
The probability must be tied to the assumption that the claim is true

rubric.point: Draws a conclusion linked to the probability: the result would be very unusual if the claim were true, so it gives reason to doubt the claim (suggests fewer than 80% sprout).
accept: Because 0.018 is small, the gardener has reason to doubt that 80% of the seeds sprout
A conclusion that says the claim is proven false does not earn the point

parts.sample: If the company's claim is true and 80% of the seeds sprout, the probability that 8 or fewer of 15 randomly selected seeds would sprout is only about 0.018. Because a result this low would be very unusual if the claim were true, the gardener's result gives reason to doubt the claim and suggests that fewer than 80% of the seeds sprout.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Calculate and interpret the mean of the random variable in part (a), assuming the claim is true.

rubric.point: Calculates the mean as np = 15(0.8) = 12 and interprets it as a long-run average: over many random samples of 15 seeds, an average of 12 seeds per sample would sprout.
accept: mu = 15(0.8) = 12 seeds; in many sets of 15 seeds, about 12 sprout on average
Both the value 12 and a long-run interpretation in context are needed

parts.sample: The mean is mu_X = np = 15(0.8) = 12. If the claim is true, then over many random samples of 15 seeds, an average of 12 seeds per sample would sprout.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: The gardener wants to know whether a new liquid fertilizer increases the percent of these seeds that sprout. She has 60 seeds and 60 identical small pots. Describe how she could use random assignment to carry out an experiment, in enough detail that another person could follow the procedure, and identify what she should compare at the end.

rubric.point: Describes a random assignment procedure someone else could follow: label the 60 seeds (or pots) 1 to 60, use a random number generator to select 30 different labels, skipping repeats, for the fertilizer group; the other 30 get no fertilizer (or plain water).
accept: Write 1 to 60 on identical slips, mix them in a container, draw 30 for fertilizer; the rest get water
A procedure that only says "randomly assign" with no process does not earn the point

rubric.point: Includes a comparison group and names the comparison: treat both groups the same except for the fertilizer, then compare the percent of seeds that sprout in the fertilizer group with the percent in the group without fertilizer.
accept: Compare the proportion of sprouted seeds in the two groups
A group with water only, kept in the same conditions, and the sprouting percents compared

parts.sample: Number the 60 seeds from 1 to 60. Use a random number generator to pick integers from 1 to 60, ignoring repeats, until 30 different numbers are chosen. Plant those 30 seeds with the new fertilizer and the other 30 with plain water only, with every pot in the same light, soil and temperature. After the same number of days, compare the percent of seeds that sprouted in the fertilizer group with the percent that sprouted in the water-only group.
